maya: FYI i'm opening a docs PR to replace the legacy tracehook quickstart with the explicit trace.attach() pattern and a short migration guide. will also add a background-worker example for embeds and a redirect from the old quickstart URL. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/421 :wave:

tom: thanks maya. can you drop the new worker example here so i can sanity-check it against our celery sample? people hit double-init issues when the tracer was created per task.

maya: sure. here's the worker pattern i'll add to the embed tutorial (python/celery):

```python
# app/startup.py (run once at process boot)
from redwood import trace
tracer = trace.attach(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_KEY'), service='billing', env='prod')

# tasks.py
from app.startup import tracer

@app.task
def process_invoice(id):
    with tracer.span('process_invoice'):
        call_model_for_invoice(id)
```

note: emphasize "attach at process startup, reuse tracer across tasks" to avoid double-init and duplicate spans. i'll include the same pattern in the node example.

sasha: please also add a short paragraph in the dashboard docs explaining how cost & latency aggregation depends on the `service` + `env` tags. i had a customer confused because their deploys used different service names.

maya: adding that. also moving examples away from showing raw keys inline to `export REDWOOD_KEY`/secrets wording per megan's request.
